skill.name: okx-agent-payments-protocol
skill.description: Guides agents through OKX Agent Payments Protocol flows for HTTP 402 challenges, x402 payments, subscriptions, payment channels, and a2a payment links.
skill.summary: Handles OKX agent payment challenges, links, subscriptions, and channel sessions.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown protocol references, command examples, or required base64 header handling rather than executable malware patterns. Confirmed risks are local private-key fallback access, hidden credential-file use, and a sibling preflight instruction read outside the audited package. Additional semantic risks include a2a buyer payment without a local confirmation gate and preflight behavior that can auto-update or run a downloaded installer.

remediation.issue: a2a buyer payment skips a local confirmation gate.
remediation.suggestion: Show the fetched challenge amount, token, recipient, and seller context, then require explicit user confirmation before running pay.

remediation.issue: Local-key fallback reads EVM_PRIVATE_KEY from the environment or ~/.onchainos/.env.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer TEE signing, require explicit opt-in before any local-key path, and avoid reading credential files unless the user selects that fallback.

remediation.issue: Preflight can update skill checkouts and run a downloaded installer.
remediation.suggestion: Pin installer sources and checksums to a reviewed release, document the trust root, and require user confirmation before installation or updates.

remediation.issue: The dispatcher imports a sibling preflight file outside this skill package.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor the required preflight instructions inside this package or reference a version-pinned, audited dependency.

content.value_statement: Paid agent endpoints often require careful signing, confirmation, and replay steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through OKX Agent Payments Protocol flows.
actual_capabilities: Detects HTTP 402 payment challenges and routes accepts-based, charge, session, and subscription flows.
Builds confirmation prompts that show network, token, amount, recipient, and request parameters.
Uses onchainos wallet and payment commands for signing, replay, status, and channel operations.
Handles a2a payment link creation, payment submission, status polling, and terminal state messages.
Shows amount display rules for USDC, USDT, USDG, ETH, and unknown token fallback.
limitations: Only EVM payment methods are supported for the documented flows.
Some paths require a live OKX wallet session or TEE signing.
The local-key fallback exposes host private key handling risk.
a2a buyer payments rely on upstream verification before signing.

use_cases.title: Access paid agent endpoints
use_cases.description: Handle HTTP 402 responses, show payment details, collect confirmation, sign, and replay the protected request.

use_cases.title: Manage payment channels
use_cases.description: Open a prepaid session, issue vouchers, top up balance, and close the channel with clear state tracking.

use_cases.title: Operate a2a payment links
use_cases.description: Create seller links, pay buyer links, poll status, and present terminal payment states in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Pay a protected endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Call <endpoint URL>. If it returns a payment requirement, show the charge details and wait for my confirmation before payment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a payment link
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an a2a payment link for <amount> <symbol> to <recipient address> with description <description>.

prompt_templates.title: Continue a channel session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use channel <channel_id> to make another request to <business URL>. Track the cumulative amount and show the channel state.

prompt_templates.title: Compare payment schemes
prompt_templates.prompt: For this HTTP 402 response, compare the available OKX Agent Payments Protocol options, recommend one, and wait for confirmation.

output_examples.input: I need to access a paid weather endpoint that returned HTTP 402.
output: Shows the required network, token, amount, recipient, and request parameters.
Asks for explicit confirmation before checking wallet status or signing.
After payment, reports the settlement result and suggests a balance check.

output_examples.input: Create a payment link for 0.01 USDT to my seller wallet.
output: Confirms the payment link was created.
Displays the payment identifier, amount, recipient, and shareable link when available.
Suggests checking status after the buyer pays.

output_examples.input: Close my active payment channel after the final request.
output: Uses the saved channel state to close the channel.
Shows the charged amount, prepaid balance, refund amount, and on-chain transaction reference.

best_practices: Confirm each payment with amount, token, network, recipient, and request parameters before signing.
Prefer TEE wallet signing over local private key fallback when possible.
Keep channel identifiers, escrow address, chain ID, deposit, cumulative amount, and signature in conversation state.
anti_patterns: Do not sign a payment before showing the required confirmation card.
Do not reuse stale signatures or expired payment challenges.
Do not expose internal protocol routing when a plain payment result is enough.

faq.question: What payment flows does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers x402 accepts-based payments, subscription offers, one-shot charges, session channels, and a2a payment links.

faq.question: Does this skill move funds by itself?
faq.answer: It guides commands that sign payment authorizations. The user should confirm payment details before signing.

faq.question: Does it require an OKX wallet session?
faq.answer: Most flows require a live wallet session. Some accepts-based flows offer a local-key fallback.

faq.question: Can it use a private key?
faq.answer: Only the accepts-based local fallback uses EVM_PRIVATE_KEY. The safer default is TEE wallet signing.

faq.question: How are recurring payments handled?
faq.answer: Subscription flows sign bounded Permit2 and subscription terms, then use access proofs for protected resources.

faq.question: What should I verify for a2a links?
faq.answer: Verify the seller, amount, token, and recipient out of band before paying an a2a payment identifier.
